newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: SOCCER-"MINI" WORLD CUP COMPETITION GETS GO-AHEAD.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-"MINI" WORLD CUP COMPETITION GETS GO-AHEAD.

text.p: World governing body FIFA gave the go-ahead on Thursday to a "mini" World Cup to be contested every two years by continental champions and confirmed Saudi Arabia will host the first Confederations Cup in December next year.
Eight national teams will take part in the competition which will consist of two groups of four with the winners of each group meeting in the final.

The likely participants of the first competition will be South American champions Uruguay, CONCACAF champions Mexico, African champions South Africa, likely Oceania champions Australia, World champions Brazil, host nation Saudi Arabia, the as-yet unknown Asian champions, and either European champions Germany or the Czech Republic who finished as runners-up to Germany in this summer's European championship.

FIFA general secretary Sepp Blatter said in announcing the new competition: "It has already been staged twice unofficially. Now it is an official FIFA competition and I am sure it will certainly make its way and become very popular."
Blatter added the intention was for the tournament to be staged every two years, but that might change to four years in due course.
The first tournament is due to be staged between December 12- 21 next year and the draw for the competition would be made on February 21 next year in Riyadh.

The major doubt concerns the participation of Germany and UEFA, European soccer's ruling body, will decide at a meeting in Tenerife on December 5 whether to replace Germany with the Czech Republic if, as expected, the Germans do not take part.
Gerhard Mayer-Vorfelder, vice-president of the German Football Associatin (DFB) and a member of FIFA's executive committee, said they would not compete in the tournament.
"There is no discussion about this in Germany, the team will not compete, it is a problem with scheduling and the clubs have other commitments," he said.
The new competition falls in the middle of the German mid-winter break when many of the leading clubs take part in indoor competitions.
